seen.extent: two letters of Barry Close to Wellesley, 9 pages each; in No. 90 about four pages (pp. 4-6 of the file) and in No. 91 about two pages (pp. 7-8) carry passages in cipher, the rest is clear
seen.cipher: Numeric cipher: runs of two-digit numbers separated by full stops written in the line of the letter. Every cipher run is struck through and its plain text is written above it in another hand (No. 90: 'if Jeswunt Rao Holkar approach ... he will join'; No. 91: 'ought not to be allowed to pass entirely [without] notice', 'the Peshwa holds frequent councils ... deliberating on measures'). The decipherment is on the leaf.

1355.closed: Contemporary decipherment interlined on the leaf: in both consultation copies (Secret Cons. 23 June 1802 Nos. 90 and 91, Abhilekh Patal scans seen 11 Nov 2026) every run of cipher numbers is struck through with the plain English written above it. The two letters are a plaintext-ciphertext pair for the Poona Residency cipher, useful as key material for other Close letters, not an unread text.
